Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. She got annoyed with me and told me it would help her feel better and to grieve. We argued back and forth for a bit. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

The fiancée is now reaching out to pet shops and shelters to get another bird, even calling her aunt for money. The person tried to stop her, saying it's a bad idea right now because they just lost Rosie. They argued, and the fiancée called the person an asshole, saying they have no say in the matter. They didn't say they should never get another pet, just that they should wait until they've mourned and their finances are better. So, is the person the asshole here? Let's think about this. On one hand, the person is trying to be responsible. They're considering the financial strain of getting another bird, especially since they're the only one working and money is tight. They also don't want the fiancée to rush into getting another pet right after losing Rosie, thinking it's not healthy. They want to wait until they've both had time to grieve and maybe when their financial situation improves. On the other hand, the fiancée is grieving and feels that getting another bird would help her cope with the loss. She's reaching out to get a new bird and even asking for money from her aunt, which shows how much she wants this. The person's attempt to stop her might have come off as unsupportive, especially since the fiancée is already vulnerable due to her depression. The person feels they have a right to say something because they're the one paying the bills, and they don't want to spend money on a new pet right now. But the fiancée feels that the person has no say in the matter, which is why she called them an asshole. I think it's a tough spot for both of them. The person is trying to be responsible and considerate of their financial situation, but their approach might have been insensitive to the fiancée's emotional state. The fiancée is grieving and looking for comfort, and the person's reaction might have made her feel invalidated. Maybe the person could have approached the situation differently. Instead of outright saying "no," they could have expressed their concerns in a more supportive way, acknowledging the fiancée's pain and suggesting that they wait a bit before making any decisions. They could have offered to talk about it later when both are calmer or suggested other ways to cope with the loss. In the end, it's a delicate balance between being responsible and being supportive. The person's intentions were good, but their approach might have been too harsh, leading to an argument. So, while they weren't entirely wrong to voice their concerns, they could have handled it more sensitively.
